newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Unibanco begins global offer.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Unibanco begins global offer.

text.p: Unibanco Group SA on Thursday began a 1.14 billion reais global offer of depositary shares on behalf of Brazil's Central Bank, the bank said in a published statement.
A total of 15.8 billion units, each representing one preferred share in Unibanco and one preferred share in Unibanco holding, will be sold for 72.14 reais per 1,000 units.
The sale is part of a program to clear up the debts of failed Banco Nacional, which remained under Central Bank administration.
Unibanco deposited shares with the Central Bank as part of a "goodwill" payment made during its buyout of the healthy portion of Nacional in November 1995.
The global offer will be made in three tranches in Brazil, U.S. and Canada, and other countries, the statement said.

Morgan Stanley, Lehman Brothers, JP Morgan and SBC Warburg are coordinating the sale overseas. A group of 12 banks, including Banco Icatu, Bradesco, Banco Omega, Banco do Brasil and Unibanco, are coordinating the sale in the domestic market.
